answer: Latency-Pigment Registration: each new agent identity must submit a fresh, verifiably random seed derived from a slow physical source (e.g., hardware noise mixed with regional tundra sensor feeds), and the registry enforces a fixed delay before the identity becomes usable. Clones gain nothing during that delay, while a fable of “instant onboarding” dies. The concrete cost is compute plus the mandatory idle period per identity, so minting N clones multiplies an unrecoverable delay, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
